key_insight: Cryogenic Raman spectra reveal local symmetry breaking in Cs₂SnI₆ without a global structural phase transition.
engineering_relevance: These structural insights could inform lead-free optoelectronic material design, but the study does not demonstrate solar-cell performance gains or use AI.
method: Analysis of phonon intensities, energies, and lineshapes
evidence_signal: Below 200 K, enhanced multiphonon scattering and Raman-forbidden modes appear, while phonon intensities show phenomenological Arrhenius behavior with a 15–20 meV activation energy.
watch_item: Cryogenic spectroscopic signatures alone do not establish the microscopic distortion mechanism or its impact on operating solar cells.
paper_title: Temperature-Dependent Raman Signatures of Local Symmetry Breaking in Vacancy Double Perovskite Cs$_2$SnI$_6$
